newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: GOLF-WILL TRY TO FINISH RAINY MEMORIAL AS 54-HOLE EVENT MONDAY.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-WILL TRY TO FINISH RAINY MEMORIAL AS 54-HOLE EVENT MONDAY.

text.p: Rain again kept players from being able to complete the third round of the water-logged Memorial Tournament and officials decided to try and complete the round Monday and make it a 54-hole event.
The third round was interrupted by rain for the third time Sunday afternoon when play was called for the day.
The leaders, Scott Hoch and Vijay Singh of Fiji, were tied at 12 under par through 10 holes. Australian Greg Norman was a stroke behind at 11-under after 14 holes.
More rain is forecast for Monday.
If the water-saturated course makes conditions unplayable Monday, the tournament will revert to 36 holes, and second-round leader Hoch will be declared the winner.
Hoch stood at 12 under par through 36 holes, two shots better than Tommy Tolles.
The third round was interrupted twice on Saturday, and resumed at 2:30 p.m. Sunday. The rain returned less than two hours later, flooding the course and halting play yet again.
Though the Memorial is traditionally rain plagued, with just one completely dry week in 22 years, the last Memorial to be reduced to 54 holes was in 1990, won by Norman.
"I've got to start on the 15th tee tomorrow, and try to make two birdies on the four holes to set myself up with a chance to win," said Norman on Sunday.
Norman had just holed his fourth successive birdie putt on the 14th green when play was called, but said that he was not concerned with the break in momentum.
"I've been in enough rain delays to know how to handle them," said Norman.
